questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been to Australia before and really enjoyed it! I still have a lot of friends there and family, so I thought it was a great opportunity to come back and live there for a long time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, but we were also a lot of danish people going to the same uni, which made everything easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: USYD probably had a lot of assistance, but didn't really use much of it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit difficult to navigate, time consuming and really expensive. I ended up finding something through SYDNEY BOUTIQUE SHARED HOMES with 4 girls, which was nice to have something before arriving in Sydney. I did also find some other rooms through FLATMATES (app), but ended up saying no to those. I still think it is a great place to find something, if you're fine with living alone. You can sometimes you find multiple rooms in the same house though - that's how I found the one through SYDNEY BOUTIQUE SHARED HOMES.

Recommendations:
- All housing in Sydney is pretty last minute. If you try to find something 6 months before even 2 months before, there are not a lot of options.
- If they ask you to pay a bond, you should only pay 1 week of rent according to the law
- If you wanna live close to uni Newtown is in my opinion the best option. Other cute suburbs not too far from USYD is Paddington and Surry Hills.

Some areas that could be a good option to look at:
Chippendale 
Surry hills
Paddington
Newtown (most fun)
Glebe
Annandle
Alexandria
Leichhardt 
Redfern 
marrickville (N/E) - cool place but a bit far away from beach and city center

Near the beach (it's long trip to uni though):
bondi junction (2022)
randwick (2031)
bronte (2024)
waverley (2024)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You're gonna spend a lot of time on public transport. Everything takes at least 40 min to get to. If you have a lot of days at uni, I would recommend not staying more than one hour away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too few options and too expensive...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get everything in your email from your coordinator at USYD. It is pretty easy to navigate, but the waiting time for responses can be pretty slow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had a coordinator to help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful, but one of the subjects I wanted was cancelled:(

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: HSPC1000 Bioethics is a nice and easy subject.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The subjects I chose were pretty easy and the uni is catered to help the students a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a first-year elective, HSPC1000 Bioethics, and a third-year elective, PCOL3012 Drug development and design.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The lectures are pretty boring and they treat you more like a child than they would at UCPH. It's kind of like being back in high school.
Other than that they are pretty chill and they help you a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HSPC1000 Bioethics 
PCOL3012 Drug development and design

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really recommend HSPC1000 Bioethics - It's quite simple and nice! You get a lot of credits through out the semester, so the final exam only counts for 35% of the grade. 

Drug development and design is a really interesting class if you're interested in drug development and computational modelling. It was a bit more demanding than anticipated at first, but still easier than classes I would take at KU. A lot of the big assignments are at the end of the semester which is really annoying, so I would recommend choosing a course where the assignment are more spread out, and you don't have 40 credits in the last couple of weeks of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot, but I didn't really use any of them as people were quite young.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! Running, tennis, choir, revy, caving, diving, consulting, STEM etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try surfing:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around and see Australia! I really loved my road trip in Tasmania (biggest highlight) and my trip to Uluru:) And if you need a good study break - Bali is just the place (specifically Uluwatu).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Didn't really hangout with them that much, but got a really good friend through my research group. It helps if you see them a lot!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very laid back and chill.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare to spend money! You can cheapen the exchange in a lot of ways (more oatmeal and less beers), but if you wanna travel and experience australia it's gonna be expensive. It's more fun to be able to say yes and be prepared mentally to be cashing out:)

It can get really cold if you're staying in a house in Sydney!! The houses are build awfully (no insolation and one-layered windows) and if you rent they often don't have heating. So if you're there doing winter (late fall/early spring) remember to bring warm clothes. ALSO bring a rain coat - it rains a lot.

USYD has a lot of free stuff, mostly in welcome days, but also throughout the semester so look out for that!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was a big privilege to be able to turn off all the expectations from back home and be very present at the exchange at USYD. It was so nice only having to focus on your academics, your friends and experiencing a new city. And of course all the nice new friends I made:)))

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends and family back home

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nope

questions.answer: Yes
